subject: Service tail-latency spike: mitigation steps + customer comms
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] 95/99p latency spike on /v1/generate - tentatively isolating root cause

Team —

We started seeing a tail-latency spike around 08:45 PT across a subset of requests to /v1/generate. 95th and 99th percentiles climbed ~3-4x for sequences >1024 tokens. Attaching the first diagnostic graph and a small set of sampled requests.

What we've observed: 
- Start: ~08:45 PT; spike persisted across the next ~20 minutes, then recurred at ~08:57.
- Affected callers show high queue_time and slow KV cache warm-up.
- Spike correlates with a surge of long-context requests from a single customer (NovaRetail) hitting a large-quantized model instance.
- No obvious OOMs or infra-level preemptions.

Actions taken so far:
- Rolled one replica from q4->q2 kernel variant (attempting fallback) — slight improvement but not back to baseline.
- Forced a KV cache flush for the affected pod group to reset pathological cache state; improved throughput briefly.

Immediate asks:
- Connor / Marissa: product guidance on acceptable rollback (model variant downgrade) and customer messaging.
- Maya: can we temporarily route NovaRetail to the less-optimized but lower-latency variant?
- Sean: SRE runbook step to throttle long sequences or impose short-term per-customer concurrency cap?

Attachments: latency_graph_20260322.png, sample-requests-99pct.json

Dylan
SRE (on-call)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] 95/99p latency spike on /v1/generate - tentatively isolating root cause

Thanks Dylan — good triage. Quick thoughts: 

1) Product constraints: we should avoid a global rollback. For NovaRetail specifically, routing to a lower-latency variant (q2) for a short window is acceptable as an exception, provided we track output quality. Marissa, can your team prepare a short evaluation run (50 representative prompts) comparing q4 vs q2 outputs for NovaRetail? Preferably within the hour.

2) Customer-facing: we need to give NovaRetail a succinct status note and ETA for mitigation (target 60-90m). Draft below; please iterate. I'll send it once we agree on wording.

3) Ops controls: Sean, agree with a temporary per-customer concurrency cap (suggest 8 concurrent long-context requests). If we automate this, please add a short flag for NovaRetail for 1h and monitor.

Sean/Marissa/Maya please confirm feasibility. I will prep the customer note if we have alignment.

Connor
Director, Product
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] 95/99p latency spike on /v1/generate - tentatively isolating root cause

Connor — we can run a quick quality delta. I'll pull a stratified set of ~50 in-context prompts from the sample-requests-99pct.json file and run them against q4 and q2. Give me 30-45 minutes to produce a short summary (BLEU-ish metrics + 5 spot-checks). If q2 looks acceptable, we can authorize routing.

Also: we should confirm whether NovaRetail's client is using streaming or non-streaming paths; streaming can exacerbate tail latency due to chunking. Dylan — can you confirm request metadata?

I'll standby with the eval and the short summary.

Marissa
PM, Models
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] 95/99p latency spike on /v1/generate - tentatively isolating root cause

Agree with Connor / Marissa. Quick operational plan I've applied: 
- Temporary per-customer concurrency cap applied: nova-retail-cust-id -> 8 (1h window)
- Added a routing rule to send nova-retail requests to the q2 variant pool (will only affect new sessions).
- Enabled verbose tracing for the affected pod group and forwarded the trace bundle to Dylan.

Caveats: routing to q2 will increase token cost slightly and could yield small quality deltas for long-context prompts. I'll watch error rates and 99p latency over next 30m and escalate if things worsen.

Sean
SRE Lead
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 10:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] 95/99p latency spike on /v1/generate - tentatively isolating root cause

Update: completed quick eval (attached as a short summary). Findings: 
- q2 vs q4 on 50 samples: average embedding similarity 0.92, minor tokenization differences on ~8 prompts, 3 prompts with noticeable brevity loss on q2.
- No safety or hallucination regressions observed in the sample set.

Recommendation: proceed with temporary routing to q2 for NovaRetail for up to 2 hours while SRE monitors latency and we run a more comprehensive A/B analysis. We'll prepare a note to NovaRetail explaining the temporary routing and expected impact.

Marissa

Attachment: eval-summary-novaretail-q2-vs-q4.txt
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@novaretail.com>
Cc: ops@novaretail.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service interruption: temporary routing change and next steps

Samantha —

Thanks for your patience this morning. I wanted to provide a concise update and what we did to reduce the impact you were seeing.

What happened: between ~08:45–09:10 PT we saw intermittent tail-latency spikes for long-context Gen calls tied to a concentrated burst of long sequences from a subset of your traffic. Our SRE team identified a pathological cache/warm-up behavior on the optimized kernel variant serving those requests which caused elevated 95th/99th latencies for a small percentage of calls.

What we did: 
- Temporarily routed new sessions for NovaRetail to a lower-latency model variant (q2) to restore tail latency to baseline. This is a targeted, short-duration exception for your account only.
- Applied a short concurrency cap for long-context requests to help stabilize the service while we investigate.
- Continued deeper diagnostics (traces and sampling) to identify root cause.

What to expect: 
- Immediate user impact: latency should be improved to pre-spike levels; you may see minor differences in response length on very long prompts.
- Next steps from us: we will complete a follow-up analysis and provide a post-incident summary with root cause and remediation plan within 72 hours.

We recognize the disruption and we want to make this right — we'll apply a usage credit for affected requests and notify you in the post-incident report with the estimated credit amount.

If you have any immediate questions or want to loop in your tech lead for a short call, I can be available this afternoon.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Director, Product
Redwood Inference
